title: Timeline sampling and explainable aggregation notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick brainstorm + sketch notes for a timeline-level sampling and aggregation feature that makes long traces usable without losing signal. Focus: UX affordances for sampling, how aggregated buckets expose explainable metrics, and lightweight interactions for drilling from bucket -> individual traces.

Context / problem statements:
- Some customers have very wide latencies (50ms -> 5s) with lots of low-frequency heavy tails. The current waterfall overwhelms them when looking at a 24h window (hundreds of thousands of traces).
- Existing filters (percentile, tag filters) help but are hard to combine with the visual timeline. Users want to see distribution over time and then jump to representative traces quickly.
- We must avoid hiding important edge cases when we aggregate: an aggregation that masks a rare but critical error is worse than no aggregation.

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
1) Surface high-level shape of latency distribution over arbitrary time ranges (minute/hour/day) with confidence about what the aggregated buckets represent.
2) Make sampling strategy transparent and explainable. Users should be able to see sampling parameters and toggle between modes (representative, tail-focused, random, deterministic replay).
3) Provide one-click transitions from any bucket to: a) a list of representative traces, b) a filtered trace view with the exact query that produced the bucket, c) a compare view for bucket vs baseline.
4) Keep the UI snappy — aggregated previews should be precomputed or streamed progressively.

Wireframe notes / interactions:
- Top row: time-range selector + aggregation mode dropdown (auto, percentiles, k-means, heuristic-tail). Modes explained with short tooltip text.
- Main canvas: stacked area showing count of traces over time; overlaid heatmap showing median/90/99 latency bands. Hovering a timeslice shows a small popover with: count, median, p90, p99, error-rate, sampling-mode badge.
- Timeslice bucket: bucket width adjusts based on zoom and total range; when a bucket is clicked it expands in the right rail into a "Bucket Details" panel. Panel contains: 
  * sampling method used (e.g., stratified by user, deterministic hash, random seed 42)
  * sample size vs total (X / Y)
  * sample representativeness score (0-100) with explanation of the score (heuristic: KL divergence to population, see notes below)
  * quick-actions: "List representatives", "Jump to worst trace", "Open compare"
- Representatives list: small table with 6 rows by default showing: trace id, latency, error flag, user tag, first span name, confidence score. Each row has actions: open trace, pin, add to investigation set.

Sampling modes / heuristics (sketch):
- auto: adaptive sampler that tries to preserve distribution moments (mean, variance, skew) and retains all error traces by default.
- percentile-slice: sample uniformly within each percentile bucket (e.g., sample 1 trace per p10 slice, more in p99).
- tail-focused: oversample traces above some threshold or above configured percentile. Good for debugging regressions.
- deterministic-hash: map request id -> bucket to ensure reproducible samples across time and users. Useful for reproducing alerts.
- random-seed: purely random sample when user wants unbiased estimates.

Explainability details (how we show why a sample is representative):
- Representativeness score calculation (short blurb): combine distribution similarity (KL), presence of rare spans, and error markers. Provide a link to a deeper explainer page (Confluence) and a toggle to show raw numbers used.
- When a bucket is selected show a small sparkline of span-level hotspots aggregated across sample traces (top 5 spans contributing to latency). Clicking the span drills into span timeline explorer filtered to that span signature.

Progressive loading and performance considerations:
- Initial load: fetch high-level histogram and p50/p90/p99 per timeslice (small payload).
- When hovering, fetch a lightweight timeslice summary (if not cached) with counts by status and top tags.
- On bucket expand, lazily fetch the sample set. Allow streaming of representative list rows.
- For very large ranges, default to summary + downsampled live preview; show an explicit control to "Scan full range (costly)" so users know query will be heavier.

Investigative workflows (common flows):
- Alert -> Open timeline at alert time -> switch to tail-focused sampling -> click bucket -> open "Worst trace" -> create investigation set (pins) -> run compare vs baseline range.
- Ad-hoc exploration: open 24h range -> pick hour with spike -> view representatives -> filter by route tag -> open waterfall with prefix cache highlights.

Open questions / risks:
- How to store deterministic-hash mapping for private deployments with very high cardinality request IDs? (cost vs value tradeoff).
- UX for communicating sampling bias to non-technical users — what phrasing avoids confusion but is accurate?
- SLA/Cost implications of "Scan full range" action and how to gate it for free-tier customers.
- Need to define exact math for representativeness score that's both robust and computable quickly. Potential approach: small streaming summary + online KL estimate.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Spike on backend: prototype small API that returns p50/p90/p99 per timeslice + representative trace candidates (deadline: 2025-11-18) — owner: Marco
- [ ] Create visual mockups for: a) timeslice popover, b) bucket details rail, c) representatives table (deadline: 2025-11-25) — owner: Helen
- [ ] Write short technical note on representativeness metric and deterministic sampling tradeoffs; link to PR where sampling will be surfaced (owner: Devon)
- [ ] Add UX copy suggestions for tooltips and sampling explanations, short A/B text variants to test clarity

Notes from sync with infra (2025-11-07):
- Precomputing p50/p90/p99 per minute for 90 days is feasible if we do rolling summaries and compress them. Storage estimate: ~60GB across tenant partitions (rough ballpark).
- Streaming sample candidate generation might be best-effort with fallback to async job for very large buckets.

Quick mock copy ideas (for tooltips):
- "Representative sample: a small set of traces that reflect the distribution in this time window. We keep error traces to ensure issues aren't missed."
- "Deterministic sample: the same requests will be chosen each time (useful for reproducible investigations)."

References / links:
- JIRA-RT-4123 (sampling API spike)
- github.com/redwood-inference/console PR#788 (initial histogram UI commit)
